disease_label_per_paper: Non-cirrhotic ascites due to severe alcoholic hepatitis
presentation_summary: 36-year-old non-obese woman with alcohol use disorder presented with one week of constipation, abdominal distension, productive cough, and non-bloody vomiting after escalation in drinking two weeks before the hospital visit.
Exam showed extensive jaundice, diffuse abdominal distension with positive fluid wave, tenderness, slow speech/confusion but preserved orientation, and tachycardia to 105 bpm.

Admission labs showed MCV 107 fL, albumin 3.0 g/dL, AST 153 U/L, ALT 43 U/L, total bilirubin 9.1 mg/dL, ALP 186 U/L, INR 1.7, ammonia 76 umol/L, sodium 134 mmol/L, creatinine 0.37 mg/dL, MELD-Na 24, and MDF 42.2.

Viral/autoimmune/Wilson/hemochromatosis workup, Doppler evidence of no cirrhosis or thrombosis, paracentesis culture/SAAG interpretation, treatment response, and final case diagnosis are confirmatory/non-ranking.

quality_warnings: Ascites, cough/infection concern, mild encephalopathy, and steatosis imaging are preserved as presentation evidence.
Negative etiologic workup, paracentesis culture/SAAG interpretation, non-cirrhotic adjudication, treatment response, and outcome are confirmatory/non-ranking.
This case keeps non-cirrhotic ascites as an alcoholic-hepatitis manifestation/context, not a disease-name qualifier.
